title: A change runs with relay's settings from the project only
what: A change cycle reads relay's settings, rules and tools from the project (and relay's pinned copy) instead of the user's global relay and Claude Code settings, so the same commit gives the same gate result on this Mac and in a clean container; the 23 pieces of global state are each removed, moved into the project, or named as a required input.
why: Owner, 26-27 Oct: "Как мы вообще планируем задачи, документируем эксперименты, мы должны быть устройство независимым, вплоть до того что бы можем запускать каждое изменение в новой docker контейнере где предустановлены все необходимые утилиты, как будто это запуск ci/cd в стандартных системах (woodpecker), с минимумом настроек глобального relay, хочу вообще без глобальных настроек relay и claude, полностью чистое окружение с предустановленными утилитами и файлами проекта / При этом получать тот же результат". Owner's answers to the clean-environment design rev 2, 27 Oct: "3. A" (this Mac re-gates until 3 waves in a row agree with the container, then the container's gate decides), "4. A" (plans and same-setup work right after the scripts move; containers after the metrics build). Measured 27 Oct: 23 pieces of global state a change cycle depends on (6 fail without it, 11 differ, 3 do not care, 3 not verified); setup fingerprint differs on 8 of 10 lines between this Mac and a clean container. Design recommendation B (relay project-local on the host) first, then A (a container per change). Design source: scratchpad report design-clean-env.md rev 2, 27 Oct; redo against the fresh repository when taken. IP 95 chosen by the front from the owner's "4. A" (agent-chosen). Queued late: recorded only in the handover until the owner asked for the plans' status.

fact: Migration 27 Oct: the link in `why` line 1 points to a session file (`design-clean-env.md` revision 2 of 27 Oct, in the session session folder; a copy is in relay's backup folder on the owner's Mac), which is deleted when the machine restarts; the facts it held that this item rests on are the notes below.

Design 27 Oct (clean-environment design, revision 2, section 8): do B first, then A. B = relay becomes project-local on the host (plugins, rules and settings come from the project's own repository); A = a container per change. B is the precondition of A: A without B is either a container with no plugins, rules or memory, or a container with the host's ~/.claude copied in, which is global settings in a box.

Measured 27 Oct: a container starts in 0.33-0.52 s cached and a clone takes 1.51 s, against a 215-935 s gate; the quick gate on one tree was green on the host and gave 25 failures and 17 errors in a container; two causes are relay defects: `ps` missing (18 errors) and `sum([0.1]*100)`, which is 10.0 on Python 3.14 and 9.99999999999998 on 3.11.

Measured 27 Oct: what a change depends on differs on 8 of 10 lines of the global-state table (plugins switched on, marketplace path, model and effort, permissions, rules text, memory, old agents and hooks, ledger, gate slots, test times); a fresh container without the plugins runs no hooks and no typed agents, so merges go unguarded and nothing is recorded.

Decided in that design (the owner can reverse each): the front and the landing stay on the host; containers run build, gate, review, fix and check but never land, take the default branch or build a train; no `--bare`; the rule files and the run's settings are generated per run and never committed; one exact Python 3.14.6 for the gate on the host and in the image; no paid runs in a container (RELAY_PAID=off). Not verified: that the Workflow tool and the InstructionsLoaded hook work under `claude -p`; that a directory marketplace accepts a relative path in project settings.
Edited where: folder entry named as a file (plugins/core is now plugins/relay; hooks.json is the file that lists the hooks a change run loads)

question: How does a Claude Code session in a relay project become project-only (plugins, rules, agents and memory from the project, not from ~/.claude)?
options: a. a shell function: `claude` in a relay project goes through relay's launcher; IDE and desktop-app sessions stay as today and are told so (recommended; about 245 agent minutes)
b. a separate command the owner types, `relay session`; plain `claude` stays global
c. project files only, no launcher; user rules, memory, agents and skills still load (about 45 agent minutes)

question: Where does a project's Claude Code memory (37 notes for relay today, kept under the user folder, keyed to this Mac's path) live?
options: a. stays where Claude Code keeps it, recorded by hash in every run (recommended by the design: the gate never reads memory)
b. saved into the project's git by one relay command, copied in at session start (about 60 agent minutes; travels to other machines and containers)

question: Where does the owner's grilling skill (today in ~/.claude/skills, not loaded by a project-only session) live?
options: a. moves into relay's front plugin, versioned with relay (recommended by the design); gone outside relay unless copied back
b. stays personal; the launcher passes the user skills folder through

reading: Point 4: not a. Grilling stays outside relay, like OpenSpec: relay ships nothing for it (relay's code never names it; only this item and the handover do). How a project-only session reaches it (a project that wants it keeps its own copy, or the launcher passes the owner's personal skills through) is a follow-up question. Points 2 and 3 are questions about the session and memory questions, not answers; point 1 confirms the Linux comparison trade-off.
